dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection: armsInterventionsModule interventions and armGroups: "Participants will receive 100 milligram (mg) guselkumab administered as a 100 milligram per milliliter (mg/mL) solution in a single-use prefilled syringe (PFS) assembled in a SelfDose device at Weeks 0, 4, 12, 20, and 28; liquid placebo for guselkumab 100 mg at Week 16 to maintain the study blind." "Partcipants will receive placebo at Weeks 0, 4, and 12 followed by guselkumab 100 mg at Weeks 16, 20, and 28." "Guselkumab" "Participants will receive 100 mg of Guselkumab as 100 mg/mL solution via SelfDose device." "Placebo" "Participants will receive matching placebo supplied in a PFS assembled in a SelfDose device." "Participants received placebo matched to guselkumab subcutaneous (SC) injection at weeks 0, 4, and 12 during placebo-controlled period." "Participants received guselkumab 100 mg SC injection at weeks 0, 4, 12, 20 and 28." -- Registry intervention descriptions are copied verbatim. Dose timing is arm-specific: Group 1 receives guselkumab at Weeks 0, 4, 12, 20, and 28 and placebo at Week 16; Group 2 receives placebo at Weeks 0, 4, and 12 then guselkumab at Weeks 16, 20, and 28. The typed dosing_periods field only represents continuous ranges, so it is left empty rather than combining those distinct discrete schedules. The registry identifies guselkumab as a solution delivered with the SelfDose device and describes subcutaneous injections in its result-group schedules. The matching placebo is described as liquid in a prefilled syringe but is not assigned a more specific dose_form enum.

severity_criteria.source_excerpt: Section 4.1 Inclusion Criteria and Section 3 population description: "moderate to severe plaque-type psoriasis defined by PASI ≥12, IGA ≥3, and involved body surface" "area ≥10%." "Inclusion Criteria" "Each potential subject must satisfy all of the following criteria to be enrolled in the study:" "3." "Have a PASI ≥12 at screening and at baseline." "4." "Have an IGA ≥3 at screening and at baseline." "5." "Have an involved BSA ≥10% at screening and at baseline." -- The protocol explicitly calls the disease moderate to severe. Criteria 3–5 require PASI ≥12, IGA ≥3, and BSA ≥10% at both screening and baseline; IGA/PASI/BSA are separate thresholds.

prohibited_concomitant: Topical therapies that could affect psoriasis or IGA evaluation (including corticosteroids, tar, anthralin, calcipotriene, tazarotene, methoxsalen, pimecrolimus, tacrolimus, and traditional Taiwanese, Korean, or Chinese medicines) during the study

Systemic or phototherapy antipsoriatic medications during the study, including steroids, conventional systemic therapies that could affect psoriasis or IGA evaluation, TNFα-targeted drugs, and IL-12/IL-17/IL-23-targeted drugs
permitted_concomitant: Shampoos containing tar or salicylic acid and topical moisturizers for psoriasis
value.population_note: Psoriasis treatment restrictions apply during the study. For conditions other than psoriasis, the protocol says every effort should be made to keep subjects on stable concomitant medications.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 8.1 Concomitant Medications for Treatment of Psoriasis and Section 8.2: "Concomitant Medications for Treatment of Psoriasis" "Topical therapies that could affect psoriasis or the IGA evaluation (eg, corticosteroids, tar," "anthralin, calcipotriene, tazarotene, methoxsalen, pimecrolimus, tacrolimus, or traditional" "Taiwanese, Korean, or Chinese medicines) are not permitted at any time during the study." "only allowable concomitant treatments for psoriasis throughout the study are shampoos" "(containing tar or salicylic acid only) and topical moisturizers." "Systemic or Phototherapy for Psoriasis" "The use of systemic or phototherapy antipsoriatic medications is not permitted at any time during" "the study." "These medications include steroids, any conventional systemic therapy that could" "affect psoriasis or the IGA evaluation (including but not limited to methotrexate, cyclosporine," "acitretin), those targeted for reducing TNFα (including but not limited to adalimumab," "infliximab, etanercept), drugs targeted for reducing IL-12, IL-17, or IL-23 (including but not" "limited to ustekinumab, tildrakizumab [MK3222], risankizumab [BI-655066], secukinumab" "Concomitant Medications for Conditions Other Than Psoriasis" "Every effort should be made to keep subjects on stable concomitant medications." "Guselkumab 100 mg and liquid placebo for guselkumab will be provided in a single-use prefilled syringe" " Group I (n=60): guselkumab 100 mg at Weeks 0, 4, 12, 20, and 28; placebo at Week 16 to maintain" -- No monotherapy or combination-background regimen is asserted: the protocol describes prohibited and permitted psoriasis concomitant therapies but does not name the randomized design as monotherapy. Pre-randomization washout criteria are not used as treatment-period restrictions; the restrictions above are explicitly stated to apply during study.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: Sections 5.1.1 Level of Significance and 5.1.1.1 Multiplicity Adjustment for Testing Procedures: "All statistical procedures to test superiority hypotheses will be performed at a 2-sided" "significance level of 0.05." "This study is designed to maintain an overall Type I error of 0.05 or" "less for the primary analysis and major secondary analyses." "5.1.1.1." "Multiplicity Adjustment for Testing Procedures" "There are 2 co-primary endpoints in this study:" " The proportion of subjects who achieve an IGA score of cleared (0) or minimal (1) at" "Week 16" " The proportion of subjects who achieve a PASI 90 response at Week 16" "Both of the co-primary endpoint analyses will be compared between the guselkumab treatment" "group and the placebo group and tested at a 2-sided α-level of 0.05." "If one of the comparisons is" "not significant at the 2-sided α-level of 0.05, the co-primary endpoints will be considered not" "In addition, there are 2 major secondary endpoints in this study to be compared between the" "guselkumab 100 mg group and the placebo group:" " The proportion of subjects who achieve an IGA score of cleared (0) at Week 16." " The proportion of subjects who achieve a PASI 100 response at Week 16." "The analyses of the major secondary endpoints will be performed only if both primary analyses" "are significant, and will be performed in the fixed sequence testing approach1, as specified" "above." "If a given comparison is not significant at the 2-sided α-level of 0.05 for superiority" "hypotheses, the remaining treatment group comparisons in this sequence will be considered not" -- The SAP states overall Type I error ≤0.05 for primary and major secondary analyses. Both co-primary endpoints are tested at two-sided 0.05; major secondary endpoints are tested only if both primary tests are significant, in the stated fixed order (IGA cleared, then PASI 100). `serial_gatekeeping` represents that explicit gate and sequence. SAP presence alone is not treated as proof the plan was finalized. The selected SAP text explicitly states overall Type I error control and the condition that both co-primary tests must pass before the sequence; these statements support the two boolean assertions.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Protocol Sections 3.1, 9.1.4–9.1.5 and Table 1 Time and Events Schedule: "Table 1: Time and Events Schedule" "Phase Placebo-Controlled Period Guselkumab Treatment Period Follow-upb" "Week Screening 0" "4 8 12 16 20 24 28 32 40" "a: The screening visit should occur within approximately 4 weeks prior to the Week 0 visit." "b: Week 40 assessments should be completed at least 12 weeks after the last study drug administration for subjects who discontinue study treatment or withdraw" " Group I (n=60): guselkumab 100 mg at Weeks 0, 4, 12, 20, and 28; placebo at Week 16 to" " Group II (n=15): placebo at Weeks 0, 4, and 12; cross over to guselkumab 100 mg at" "Week 28 is the last dosing visit; subjects will be followed for an additional 12 weeks and have a" "final safety visit at Week 40." " Group I (n=60): guselkumab 100 mg at Weeks 0, 4, 12, 20, and 28; placebo at Week 16 to" " Group II (n=15): placebo at Weeks 0, 4, and 12; cross over to guselkumab 100 mg at" "Week 4 through Week 12 (placebo-controlled period) and Week 16 through Week 32" "(guselkumab treatment period)" "Subjects will be followed for safety, efficacy, PK, and immunogenicity information through" "week 40 as indicated in the Time and Events Schedule." -- The protocol gives screening approximately four weeks before Week 0 (28 days is the exact week-to-day conversion, retaining the source's approximation). The schedule table includes study visits at Weeks 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, and 40. The phase boundary is Week 32: Week 28 is the last dosing visit, followed by the Week 40 safety visit. The 12-week follow-up duration is measured from last dose at Week 28 to Week 40; the named follow-up phase begins after the guselkumab treatment period ends at Week 32. The protocol includes a full per-visit Time and Events Schedule table.

published_results.source_excerpt: Section 14.1 Clinical Studies in Plaque Psoriasis, Trial PsO4: "14 CLINICAL STUDIES 14.1 Clinical Studies in Plaque Psoriasis Adults with Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis Four multicenter, randomized, double-blind trials (PsO1 [NCT02207231], PsO2 [NCT02207244], PsO3 [NCT02203032], and PsO4 [NCT02905331]) enrolled subjects 18 years of age and older with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who were eligible for systemic therapy or phototherapy." "Both trials assessed the responses at Week 16 compared to placebo for the two co-primary endpoints: the proportion of subjects who achieved an IGA score of 0 (" "cleared" ") or 1 (" "minimal" "Trial PsO4 Trial PsO4 [NCT02905331] evaluated the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of TREMFYA administered with the One-Press injector." "In this trial, 78 subjects were randomized to receive either TREMFYA (100 mg at Weeks 0 and 4 and every 8 weeks thereafter) [N=62], or placebo [N=16]." "The co-primary endpoints were the same as those for trials PsO1 and PsO2." "A greater proportion of subjects in the guselkumab group achieved an IGA score of 0 or 1 or a PASI 90 response at Week 16 (81% and 76%, respectively) than in the placebo group (0% for both endpoints)." "The proportion of subjects who achieved an IGA score of 0 at Week 16 was higher in the guselkumab group compared to the placebo group (56% vs." "0%)." -- Trial PsO4 is explicitly identified as NCT02905331; label values are printed percentages for the two co-primary Week 16 endpoints (IGA 0/1 and PASI 90). The label states 78 randomized with 62 TREMFYA and 16 placebo, but does not give efficacy analysis denominators or name an analysis population for these percentages, so those nullable fields remain null. The percentages are copied as printed, not computed. Arm IDs map to the existing Guselkumab (OG001) and Placebo (OG000) labels in base.json. The label explicitly prints these outcome percentages, so rate_is_derived is false. The first stated co-primary outcome maps to primary endpoint position 1 (IGA 0/1); the second maps to position 2 (PASI 90), in the order stated in the label.
